title: Configuring EUNs for Cloud App Control

blocks.text: You can customize the Zscaler Client Connector-based notifications displayed to end users when a Cloud App Control policy is triggered by their activity. For example, if your policy blocks users from interacting with or uploading files to AI and ML applications, you can display a notification to users explaining the policy violation when the block occurs. The end user notifications (EUN) are supported only for Block rules under specific conditions where application access is allowed, but certain interactions with the application are blocked (for example, viewing a social networking site is allowed, but posting content is blocked).

These EUNs are triggered by Zscaler service based on your policy configuration and are delivered by Zscaler Client Connector installed on users' endpoints. The Zscaler service provides a default notification for the Cloud App Control policy. You can also create custom messages and associate distinct notifications with individual Cloud App Control rules based on context. To learn more, see About Zscaler Client Connector-Based End User Notifications.
To create a custom notification message:

blocks.item: From the navigation menu, go to Administration > End User Notification > End User Notifications.
Select the Client Connector tab.
Click Add Custom Message.
The Add Custom Message drawer appears.
In the Add Custom Message drawer:
Under General:
Name: Enter a unique name for the custom message.
Channel: Select Cloud Application.

Under Message, select the language in which you want to customize the notification message from the drop-down menu. A preconfigured message appears for the Block policy action in the selected language.

In the Block field, you can customize the notification message that appears when an end user's activity triggers a Cloud App Control rule and the service blocks the activity. The EUN is supported only for Block rules of the Cloud App Control policy under specific conditions. To learn more, see Adding Rules to the Cloud App Control Policy.

You can embed links in the message content by using the following format: __url[Link text | example.com] (note the double underscore at the beginning). For example, __url[Learn more | https://acme.com/policy]. You can also introduce line breaks in the message content by using the //n character.
When the preconfigured message is modified, a Reset All option that allows you to restore the original message appears.
Under Additional Information, select the matched rule details that you want to display in the notification:
Destination: Include the destination IP address or domain name that triggered the rule.
Rule Name: Include the name of the triggered rule.
App Activity: Include the user activity performed in the cloud application that triggered the rule.
URL: Include the URL that triggered the rule.
App Category: Include the cloud application's category that triggered the rule.
Under Preview, you can view your configured notification message. You can view the full notification by clicking Show more.
The notification preview also includes the customization made under Settings, which are general settings applicable to all Zscaler Client Connector-based EUNs.
See image.
Click Save and activate the change.

blocks.text: You can edit custom notification messages, but the Channel field cannot be modified.

After customizing the notification message, you must enable the EUN for a Cloud App Control rule and associate the appropriate notification message. To learn more, see the Step-by-Step Configuration Guide for Zscaler Client Connector-Based EUNs.
